mainTopic: Stories of grooms who found no blood of בתולים, the new משנה on the amount of the כתובה, and word-readings starting from אלמנה
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier point: the cloth test used in ארץ ישראל can't work in בבל, because the stone used in גיהוץ would scrape the blood away. Next come three stories of grooms who found no blood. רבן גמליאל בר רבי uses a wine-barrel test, first tried on two שפחות, to show a bride is still a בתולה. רבן גמליאל הזקן confirms that the women of the דורקטי family have no blood at all. רבי sees that a starving couple's bodies were dried out, and once they are fed, blood appears. Along the way the גמרא discusses whether lacking blood is a blessing or a loss. Then a new משנה sets the כתובה at 200 for a בתולה and a מנה for a widow. The גמרא explains, through רב חנא בגדתאה, that the word אלמנה comes from מנה. It then brings more of his sayings, about rain and dates, along with word-readings of מזבח, דשא, דרגא and פוריא. The amud ends with the start of a statement by רב נחמן בר יצחק that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Our cleaning method would erase the evidence
steps.stepSummary: The cloth test from ארץ ישראל can't be used in בבל, because the גיהוץ used in בבל relies on a stone that scrapes away any blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our calendering is like their laundering. And if you say, 'Let's do calendering,' the stone will remove it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining why people in בבל can't use the cloth test that was used in ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ארץ ישראל, plain כיבוס (laundering) was enough to check a cloth. In בבל, clothes only got that clean through גיהוץ, which means rubbing them with a stone. If you used גיהוץ on the cloth, the stone would scrape off the very blood you were trying to check, so the test would prove nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: Calendering: rubbing cloth with a stone to clean or smooth it

phrases.english: Our calendering is like their laundering.
phrases.notes: "Our" means בבל and "their" means ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: And if you say: let us do calendering —
the stone removes it.
phrases.notes: Literally, the stone takes it away. The blood mark gets scraped off along with the dirt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers a question from just before this section: why don't we in בבל use the cloth test used in ארץ ישראל?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The cleaning method of בבל, גיהוץ, uses a stone that would remove the blood, so the test can't work there.
steps.whatToRemember: The test can't be used in בבל because the only cleaning method strong enough there would destroy the evidence.

steps.title: A groom and bride bring opposite claims to רבן גמליאל בר רבי
steps.stepSummary: A man tells רבן גמליאל בר רבי that he found no blood. His bride says she is still a בתולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man came before רבן גמליאל בר רבי and said: 'רבי, I was with her and found no blood.' She said: 'רבי, I am still a בתולה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story. It sets up the case so we can see how רבן גמליאל בר רבי will decide it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The groom's claim suggests she was not a בתולה. Her answer is unusual: she doesn't say the blood was missing for some other reason. She says she is still a בתולה right now. That claim can be checked, and the next step shows how.

keyTerms.meaning: A certain person who came before (a story opener)

phrases.aramaic: הַהוּא דַּאֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל בַּר רַבִּי,
phrases.english: A certain man who came before Rabban Gamliel son of Rabbi,

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: רַבִּי, בָּעַלְתִּי וְלֹא מָצָאתִי דָּם.
phrases.english: said to him: My teacher, I had relations and did not find blood.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרָה לֵיהּ: רַבִּי, עֲדַיִין בְּתוּלָה אֲנִי.
phrases.english: She said to him: My teacher, I am still a virgin.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַהוּא דַּאֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל בַּר רַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the cloth test to a story about another way of checking a bride's claim.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the case: the groom says he found no blood, and the bride says she is still a בתולה.

steps.title: The wine-barrel test proves she is a בתולה
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל first tests the method on two שפחות, one a בתולה and one a בעולה, then tests the bride. The test shows she is a בתולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: 'Bring me two maidservants, one a בתולה and one a בעולה.' They brought them, and he sat them on the opening of a wine barrel. From the בעולה, the smell came through. From the בתולה, it did not. He also sat this bride on it, and the smell did not come through. He told the groom: 'Go, take possession of your acquisition.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל first checks that the wine-barrel test really works, using two שפחות. Then he uses it on the bride and rules that she is a בתולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test works like this: with a בעולה, the smell of the wine passes through, and with a בתולה it does not. Because the bride's result matched the בתולה, her claim is proven true. He tells the groom she is a proper wife, and the groom's complaint fails.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who is not a virgin
Its smell spreads or comes through
Take possession of your acquisition (keep your wife, all is fine)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶן: הָבִיאוּ לִי שְׁתֵּי שְׁפָחוֹת,
phrases.english: He said to them: Bring me two maidservants,
one a virgin and one a non-virgin.

phrases.aramaic: הֵבִיאוּ לוֹ, וְהוֹשִׁיבָן עַל פִּי חָבִית שֶׁל יַיִן,
phrases.english: They brought them to him, and he sat them on the opening of a barrel of wine.
The non-virgin: its scent came through.
The virgin: its scent did not come through.

phrases.aramaic: אַף זוֹ הוֹשִׁיבָה וְלֹא הָיָה רֵיחָהּ נוֹדֵף.
phrases.english: He sat this one too, and its scent did not come through.
phrases.notes: "This one" is the bride from the story.

phrases.english: He said to him: Go, take possession of your acquisition.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶן: הָבִיאוּ לִי שְׁתֵּי שְׁפָחוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story by showing how רבן גמליאל settled the dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The wine-barrel test showed the bride was a בתולה, so the groom must accept her.

steps.title: Why not test the bride right away?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבן גמליאל bothered with the two שפחות instead of testing the bride from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him test her directly from the beginning!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the story: if he knew the test, why did he need to try it on two other women first?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Testing the שפחות first seems like an unnecessary extra step. The question pushes us to find a reason for it, and the answer comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him check (a challenge: why didn't he?)

phrases.english: But let him examine her from the start?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how רבן גמליאל went about the test in the story.
steps.kashyaTarget: The extra trial on the two שפחות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If he knew the method, testing the bride first would have been enough, so the trial run seems unnecessary.

steps.title: He knew the test only in theory and didn't want to shame her for nothing
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל had learned the method but had never seen it done. He was not sure he could carry it out correctly, and it is wrong to put a Jewish woman through something degrading if it might not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: He had heard the teaching, but he had never seen it done. He thought he might not know exactly how to do it properly, and it is not proper to degrade Jewish women for nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. The trial run made sure the test worked before putting the bride through it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Knowing something from learning is different from having seen it done. If he had tested the bride and the method failed, he would have embarrassed her for no reason. Checking first on the שפחות protected her dignity.

keyTerms.meaning: He had heard it as a teaching
He had not seen it done in practice
He is certain, he knows well
To degrade, to treat with disrespect

phrases.english: He had heard it as a learned tradition,
but he had not seen it in practice,
and he thought: perhaps he is not certain
of the details of the matter well enough,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָאו אוֹרַח אַרְעָא לְזַלְזוֹלֵי בִּבְנוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל.
phrases.english: and it is not proper conduct to degrade Jewish women.

steps.triggerLanguage: גְּמָרָא הֲוָה שְׁמִיעַ לֵיהּ, מַעֲשֶׂה לָא הֲוָה חָזֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains a reason for the extra trial run
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The trial on the שפחות seemed unnecessary.
steps.terutzMaskana: It was needed to confirm the method first, so the bride would not be degraded for nothing.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how careful a דיין must be with a woman's dignity, even while investigating a dispute.
steps.whatToRemember: He tested the method first because he had never seen it done and didn't want to shame the bride for no reason.

steps.title: A bride claims her family has no such blood
steps.stepSummary: Another groom comes to רבן גמליאל הזקן saying he found no blood. The bride explains that she comes from the דורקטי family, whose women have neither blood of נדה nor blood of בתולים.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man came before רבן גמליאל הזקן and said: 'רבי, I was with her and found no blood.' She said: 'רבי, I am from the דורקטי family, who have neither blood of נדה nor blood of בתולים.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a second story with the same complaint but a different defense from the bride.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the bride does not claim she is still a בתולה. Instead, she gives a reason why no blood would appear: in her family, women naturally don't have this blood. A claim about a family can be checked, as the next step shows.

keyTerms.meaning: רבן גמליאל the Elder, an earlier sage than רבן גמליאל בר רבי

phrases.aramaic: הַהוּא דַּאֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל הַזָּקֵן,
phrases.english: A certain man who came before Rabban Gamliel the Elder

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: רַבִּי, בָּעַלְתִּי וְלֹא מָצָאתִי דָּם,
phrases.english: said to him: My teacher, I had relations and did not find blood.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרָה לוֹ: רַבִּי, מִמִּשְׁפַּחַת דּוֹרְקְטִי אֲנִי,
phrases.english: She said to him: My teacher, I am from the Dorketi family,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין לָהֶן לֹא דַּם נִדָּה וְלֹא דַּם בְּתוּלִים.
phrases.english: who have neither menstrual blood nor blood of virginity.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַהוּא דַּאֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל הַזָּקֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second story with the same complaint but a different defense.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the case: the bride says her family naturally has no blood of נדה or בתולים.

steps.title: Her relatives confirm the claim, and the groom is told he is fortunate
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל checks the bride's female relatives, finds she was telling the truth, and tells the groom he is lucky to marry into the דורקטי family.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל checked her relatives and found it was as she said. He told the groom: 'Go, take possession of your acquisition. Fortunate are you that you merited the דורקטי family.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל checks the bride's claim through her family, confirms it, and rules in her favor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since her female relatives really had no such blood, the missing blood proves nothing against her. He even calls the groom fortunate, because in this family blood will never cause him problems.

phrases.aramaic: בָּדַק רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל בִּקְרוֹבוֹתֶיהָ, וּמָצָא כִּדְבָרֶיהָ.
phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel examined her relatives and found it as she said.
He said to him: Go, take possession of your acquisition.
Fortunate are you that you merited the Dorketi family.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּדַק רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל בִּקְרוֹבוֹתֶיהָ, וּמָצָא כִּדְבָרֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the second story with the investigation and the ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The bride's family claim was confirmed through her relatives, so the groom's complaint fails.
steps.whatToRemember: In both stories the בית דין checks the bride's claim, once by a test and once through her family, and both times her claim is upheld.

steps.title: What does the name דורקטי mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the family name דורקטי from the previous story.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'דורקטי' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask what the strange family name דורקטי means. This sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name came up in the story about רבן גמליאל and the bride with no blood. Knowing what the name means will show whether this family trait is something good or bad.

keyTerms.meaning: The name of the bride's family, whose women had no blood

phrases.english: What is 'Dorketi'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the family name from steps 6 and 7 means.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the name דורקטי.

steps.title: דורקטי means a cut-off generation
steps.stepSummary: The name means דור קטוע, a generation that is cut off.
steps.simpleTranslation: It means a cut-off generation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that דורקטי is really two words, דור קטוע, meaning a cut-off generation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name hints that this family's line gets cut short. That already suggests that having no blood may not be a blessing, which רבי חנינא says openly next.

phrases.english: A cut-off generation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: דורקטי = דור קטוע, a generation that is cut off.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל's comfort was empty
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא says רבן גמליאל only gave the groom empty comfort.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא said: רבן גמליאל comforted that man with empty comfort.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא says that when רבן גמליאל told the groom he was lucky, it was not real good news. It was just words to make him feel better.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 7, רבן גמליאל seemed to praise the דורקטי family. רבי חנינא says that praise was hollow, because lacking blood is actually a drawback. The proof comes in the next step.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina said:
With empty comfort
did Rabban Gamliel comfort that man.
phrases.notes: 'That man' is the groom from step 7, who was told he was lucky to marry into this family.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: תַּנְחוּמִים שֶׁל הֶבֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the meaning of the name to judge רבן גמליאל's words.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן גמליאל's words to the groom were only comfort; lacking blood is not truly good.

steps.title: Proof that blood is good for a woman
steps.stepSummary: Two ברייתות show that blood is good for a woman and is linked to having many children.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי חייא taught: Just as leaven is good for dough, so blood is good for a woman. And it was taught in the name of רבי מאיר: Any woman whose blood is plentiful has many children.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings two teachings to support רבי חנינא: blood is good for a woman, and more blood means more children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חייא compares blood to leaven, which makes dough rise and grow. רבי מאיר adds that plenty of blood brings plenty of children. So a family with no blood would have few children, which fits the name 'cut-off generation.'

keyTerms.meaning: Leaven, sourdough starter that makes dough rise

phrases.english: As Rabbi Chiya taught:
Just as leaven is good for dough,
so blood is good for a woman.
And it was taught in the name of Rabbi Meir:
Any woman whose blood is plentiful,
her children are many.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי חנינא's claim with ברייתות.
steps.raayaObject: That lacking blood is a drawback, so the comfort was empty.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי חייא (blood like leaven) and the teaching in the name of רבי מאיר (more blood, more children).

steps.title: Two versions of what רבן גמליאל said
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה בר אבא and רבי יוסי בר אבין disagree on what exactly רבן גמליאל told the groom.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רבי ירמיה בר אבא said that he told him, 'Enjoy your acquisition.' רבי יוסי בר אבין said that he told him, 'You are stuck with your acquisition.'
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים argue about the exact words רבן גמליאל said to the groom. One version sounds positive and the other sounds negative.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the version of רבי ירמיה בר אבא, רבן גמליאל called the marriage a gain. In the version of רבי יוסי בר אבין, he hinted that the groom had a bad deal he now had to live with.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated, introducing a dispute of אמוראים
Enjoy, take possession of, your acquisition
You are stuck with (bound to) your acquisition

phrases.english: It was stated:
phrases.notes: The argument here is about what רבן גמליאל really said to the groom in step 7.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba said:
"Enjoy your acquisition," he said to him.
And Rabbi Yosei bar Avin said:
"You are stuck with your acquisition," he said to him.
phrases.notes: The letters in square brackets are the corrected wording, which makes it 'you' are stuck.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a dispute about the wording of רבן גמליאל's reply.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One version: 'זכה במקחך' (a gain). Other version: 'נתחייבת במקחך' (a loss).

steps.title: What gain is there in a wife with no blood?
steps.stepSummary: The 'stuck' version fits רבי חנינא, but the גמרא asks what benefit the 'enjoy' version could mean.
steps.simpleTranslation: It works for the one who says 'you are stuck', since that matches רבי חנינא. But for the one who says 'enjoy', what is the benefit?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says the negative version fits well with רבי חנינא. It then challenges the positive version: what is good about it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just learned that blood is good and brings children. So calling a bloodless wife a 'gain' seems to go against that. The גמרא wants to know what gain רבן גמליאל could mean.

keyTerms.meaning: It works well for, this view is fine

phrases.english: It works well for the one who says "you are stuck":
that is the view of Rabbi Chanina.
But for the one who says "enjoy",
what is the benefit?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests both versions of step 12 against רבי חנינא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view of רבי ירמיה בר אבא that רבן גמליאל said 'זכה במקחך'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If blood is good and brings children, a wife without blood seems to be a loss, not a gain.

steps.title: The gain: no doubts about נדה
steps.stepSummary: The benefit is that the husband will never face a doubt about whether his wife is a נדה.
steps.simpleTranslation: That he will never come to a doubt about נדה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the 'gain' is that this wife never has blood, so the couple never has to worry about doubtful נדה situations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if lacking blood means fewer children, it does bring one real advantage. Since she never sees blood, the husband is spared the worry and uncertainty about נדה.

keyTerms.meaning: A doubt whether the woman has the status of נדה

phrases.english: That he will not come to a doubt about נדה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points out a different benefit that makes the positive wording make sense.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A wife without blood brings no benefit at all, so 'זכה' makes no sense.
steps.terutzMaskana: The benefit is freedom from doubts about נדה, so 'זכה' fits.
steps.whatToRemember: Lacking blood has a downside (fewer children, according to רבי חנינא) and an upside (no doubts about נדה). The two versions of רבן גמליאל's words focus on different sides.

steps.title: A new case before רבי: no blood found
steps.stepSummary: A groom tells רבי he found no blood, and the bride insists she is still a בתולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man came before רבי and said: My teacher, I was with her and did not find blood. She said: My teacher, I am still a בתולה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new story. A groom complains to רבי that he found no blood, and the bride says she really is a בתולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same kind of problem as before, but with a new reason behind it. The next step shows how רבי solved it.

phrases.english: A certain man who came before Rebbi
said to him:
My teacher, I was with her and did not find blood.
She said to him:
My teacher, I am still a בתולה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a third story about a groom who found no blood. As in step 2, the bride answers that she is still a בתולה, but this time there is a different reason behind it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A groom claims no blood; the bride claims she is a בתולה.

steps.title: רבי feeds the hungry couple and blood appears
steps.stepSummary: In a famine, רבי had the couple bathed and fed; then the groom found blood, and רבי told him to enjoy his marriage.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was years of drought. רבי saw their faces were dark. He gave orders, and they brought them to the bathhouse, fed them, gave them drink, and brought them into a room. He was with her and found blood. רבי said: Go enjoy your acquisition.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי saw the couple was weak from hunger, so he had them washed and fed. Afterwards the groom found blood, and רבי told him to go enjoy his marriage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The missing blood was not because she was not a בתולה. It was because hunger had dried up her body. Once she ate and drank, the blood appeared and the bride was proven right.

phrases.english: And it was years of drought.
Rebbi saw that their faces were dark.
phrases.notes: Their faces were dark from hunger.

phrases.english: He gave orders about them, and they brought them into the bathhouse,
and fed them and gave them drink,
and brought them into a room.
He was with her, and found blood.
He said to him: Go enjoy your acquisition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how רבי solved the case from step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hunger can stop the blood of בתולים; once the bride was fed, blood appeared and she was proven a בתולה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches that 'no blood' does not always mean 'not a בתולה'. There can be a physical reason, so a בית דין must look into the situation first.

steps.title: רבי applies a פסוק about famine
steps.stepSummary: רבי reads a פסוק from איכה about famine drying up the body.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי read about them: 'Their skin is shriveled on their bones; it became dry like wood.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי closes the story by quoting a פסוק that describes how famine dries out the body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק explains in poetic language why no blood was found: hunger had made their bodies dry, like a dry stick that has no sap.

phrases.english: Rebbi read about them:
"Their skin is shriveled on their bones,
it became dry like wood."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the story with a פסוק that fits what happened.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Famine dries the body, as the פסוק describes, which explains the missing blood.

steps.title: New משנה: how much a כתובה is worth
steps.stepSummary: A בתולה's כתובה is 200 and a widow's is 100. A בתולה widowed, divorced, or a חלוצה from אירוסין still gets 200 and is subject to a virginity claim.
steps.simpleTranslation: A בתולה: her כתובה is two hundred. A widow: one hundred. A בתולה who became a widow, divorcée, or חלוצה from betrothal: their כתובה is two hundred, and a virginity claim can be made against them.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It sets the amount of the כתובה: 200 for a בתולה and 100 for a widow, and explains that a woman widowed or divorced only after אירוסין still counts as a בתולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The amount depends on whether the woman is a בתולה, not on whether she was ever betrothed. A woman whose betrothal ended before נישואין is still a בתולה, so she gets 200. For the same reason, a later husband can make a claim if she turns out not to be one.

keyTerms.meaning: The marriage contract money a wife receives
Betrothal, the first stage of marriage
A woman released from יבום through חליצה
A claim by the husband that she was not a בתולה

steps.confusionAlert: 'בתולה, אלמנה, גרושה וחלוצה' is not a list of four different women. It means a בתולה who became a widow, divorcée, or חלוצה while only betrothed.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
A בתולה: her כתובה is two hundred,
and a widow: one hundred.
A בתולה who is a widow, a divorcée, or a חלוצה
phrases.notes: This is one woman who is still a בתולה but lost her husband in one of these ways.

phrases.english: from betrothal:
their כתובה is two hundred,
and a virginity claim applies to them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the stories about בתולים claims.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בתולה gets a כתובה of 200 and a widow gets 100. A בתולה widowed, divorced, or a חלוצה from אירוסין gets 200 and is subject to a טענת בתולים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה sets the basic amounts of the כתובה that the rest of the perek builds on.

steps.title: Where does the word for widow come from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking what the word אלמנה means or comes from.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is the meaning of the word "אלמנה"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins discussing the משנה and asks why a widow is called an אלמנה. This question sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה just said a widow's כתובה is a מנה, which is 100. The גמרא wants to connect the name אלמנה to something real about her.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion section that comes after the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is "almana"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה from step 18 about a widow's כתובה of 100.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the word אלמנה means or refers to.

steps.title: A widow is named after the מנה
steps.stepSummary: רב חנא בגדתאה says that אלמנה is named after the מנה (100) of her כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנא of Baghdad said: She is called an אלמנה because of the מנה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חנא בגדתאה answers that the word אלמנה contains the word מנה, the 100 coins of her כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads אל-מנה as tied to מנה, the amount the משנה gives a widow. This is a sound-based explanation of the word, and it will be challenged next.

keyTerms.meaning: A sum of 100 זוז, a widow's כתובה

phrases.english: Rav Ḥana of Baghdad said:
"Almana" is named after the maneh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אלמנה is named after the מנה of her כתובה.

steps.title: But a widow from betrothal gets 200
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how this explanation works for a widow from אירוסין, whose כתובה is 200 and not a מנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What can be said about a widow from אירוסין?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב חנא: a widow from אירוסין is still called an אלמנה, but she gets 200, not a מנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 18 taught that a בתולה widowed from אירוסין keeps the full 200. So the name אלמנה does not match her כתובה amount, and the explanation seems to fail for her.

keyTerms.meaning: Betrothal, the first stage of marriage

phrases.english: A widow from betrothal,
what is there to say!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the explanation from step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חנא's claim that אלמנה is named after מנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A widow from אירוסין receives 200, yet she is still called אלמנה.

steps.title: The name carried over to her as well
steps.stepSummary: Since the ordinary widow was called אלמנה, the widow from אירוסין was given the same name.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since one widow is called אלמנה, this one is also called אלמנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the name was first given to the usual widow, who gets a מנה. The same name was then used for a widow from אירוסין too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name comes from the main case, a widow after נישואין. It is used for every widow even when the amount is different, so the name does not have to fit each case.

keyTerms.meaning: Since, because (one thing comes along with another)

phrases.english: Since they call this one "almana,"
phrases.notes: "This one" means a widow after full marriage, who really does get a מנה.

phrases.english: they also call that one "almana."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Carry-over of a name from the main case to a side case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The name must fit the כתובה of every widow.
steps.terutzMaskana: The name comes from the usual widow and is used for all widows.

steps.title: But the תורה already uses the word
steps.stepSummary: The תורה uses the word אלמנה before the רבנן set her כתובה at a מנה. How can the word come from מנה?
steps.simpleTranslation: What can be said about the word אלמנה that is written in the תורה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a second challenge: the word אלמנה appears in the תורה, long before the רבנן made the rule of a מנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the name comes from a rule of the רבנן, then the תורה, which came first, could not have used the name for that reason. Here the timing is the problem.

phrases.english: The "almana" that is written in the Torah,
what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלְמָנָה דִּכְתִיבָא בְּאוֹרָיְיתָא מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge to רב חנא's explanation.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חנא's explanation that אלמנה comes from מנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The מנה is a rule of the רבנן, but the תורה used the word אלמנה earlier.

steps.title: The תורה looked ahead to the רבנן's rule
steps.stepSummary: The תורה called her אלמנה because the רבנן would later set her כתובה at a מנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the רבנן were going to set a מנה for her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the תורה used the name based on what would happen in the future, when the רבנן would set a מנה for her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה uses a name that only fits once the later rule exists. This answer raises a new question, which comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Are going to, will in the future

phrases.english: Because the Rabbis are destined
to institute a maneh for her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The תורה speaks about the future
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תורה can only use names that fit at the time it was given.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תורה used the name because of the future rule of the רבנן.

steps.title: Does the תורה write about the future?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether a פסוק would really describe something that only happens later.
steps.simpleTranslation: And does a פסוק write about the future?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the answer it just gave. Would a פסוק really use a word based on something that did not exist yet?
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a challenge to the idea in step 24. The גמרא now needs to show another place where the תורה names something from the future.

phrases.english: And does a verse write for the future?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the תורה named the אלמנה after a future rule
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It seems strange for a פסוק to use a name based on something that does not exist yet.

steps.title: Proof from the river חדקל and the city of אשור
steps.stepSummary: Yes. The תורה says the חדקל flows east of אשור, and רב יוסף teaches that this אשור is the city סליקא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, as it says: "The name of the third river is חדקל, which flows east of אשור." And רב יוסף taught: אשור is סליקא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers yes and brings a proof. A פסוק in the story of creation mentions אשור, which רב יוסף says is the city of סליקא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof works only together with רב יוסף's teaching. It shows that the פסוק names a specific city, and the next step points out why that matters.

keyTerms.meaning: Taught (here, רב יוסף taught this explanation)

phrases.english: Yes, as it is written:
"And the name of the third river is Tigris;
that is the one that goes east of Asshur,"
and Rav Yosef taught:
Asshur, that is Seleucia.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 25 by bringing a proof.
steps.raayaObject: That a פסוק can describe things that will exist only in the future
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית 2:14, together with רב יוסף's teaching that אשור is סליקא

steps.title: The city did not exist yet, so the same is true of אלמנה
steps.stepSummary: סליקא did not exist at the time of creation. The תורה named it because it would exist later, and the same is true of אלמנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did that city exist then? Rather, the תורה named it because it would exist in the future. Here too, the name is used because of the future.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof. The city did not exist yet, so the תורה must be speaking about the future, and the word אלמנה works the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since a פסוק names a city that was built later, it can also use the name אלמנה because of a rule that came later. This keeps רב חנא's explanation standing.
steps.whatToRemember: רב חנא בגדתאה says אלמנה comes from מנה. The name was carried over to a widow from אירוסין, and the תורה used it because it was looking ahead to the רבנן's rule, just as it names סליקא before that city existed.

phrases.english: And did it exist?
Rather, it is because it was destined to be.
Here too, it is because of what was destined.
phrases.notes: "Here" means the word אלמנה in the תורה. It looks ahead to the מנה the רבנן would set.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי הֲוַאי אֶלָּא דַּעֲתִידָה הָכָא נָמֵי דַּעֲתִידָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the proof of step 26 and applies it to אלמנה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A פסוק can use names based on the future, so the תורה's word אלמנה can come from the מנה the רבנן set later.

steps.title: Five things rain does
steps.stepSummary: רב חנא בגדתאה lists five good things rain does for the land and its crops.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חנא of Baghdad said: Rain waters the land, soaks it, fertilizes it, improves the fruit, and makes it grow more.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the גמרא just quoted רב חנא בגדתאה, it now brings another teaching of his, this time about מטר (rain).
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new subject. It is brought only because it comes from the same רב. He lists five ways rain helps: it waters, soaks, fertilizes, refines the produce, and makes it multiply.

phrases.english: And Rav Ḥana of Baghdad said:
Rain irrigates, saturates,
and fertilizes, and refines, and causes proliferation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings another teaching of the same רב quoted in step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rain does five good things for the land and its produce.

steps.title: A פסוק that hints at the five benefits of rain
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר רבי ישמעאל (some say רב יימר בר שלמיא) shows a פסוק in תהלים that hints at these benefits of rain.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא בר רבי ישמעאל said, and some say it was רב יימר בר שלמיא: Which פסוק hints at this? "You water its ridges, settle its furrows, soften it with showers, and bless its growth."
steps.whatsHappening: Another אמורא brings a פסוק as support for רב חנא's list of what rain does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each part of the פסוק matches part of the list: "watering its ridges" means irrigating and soaking, softening with showers means fertilizing, and blessing its growth means refining and multiplying.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say (a different name for who said it)
What is the פסוק (that supports this)?

phrases.english: Rava bar Rabbi Yishmael said,
and some say it was Rav Yeimar bar Shelamya:
What is the verse?
"Watering its ridges abundantly, settling its furrows,
You make it soft with showers, You bless its growth."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a פסוק as support for step 28.
steps.raayaObject: רב חנא's list of the five benefits of rain

steps.title: The word מזבח stands for four good things
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר reads the word מזבח as a short form of four things the altar does: it removes, feeds, endears, and atones.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: מזבח: it removes, it feeds, it endears, it atones.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another explanation of a word, this time רבי אלעזר's reading of the word מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The letters of מזבח hint at four words: מזיח (removes), מזין (feeds), מחבב (makes Israel beloved to ה׳), and מכפר (atones). This list sets up a question in the next step.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
"Mizbe'aḥ": it moves away, and it sustains,
phrases.notes: Each word starts with a letter of מזבח: מ and ז from the first two, ב from מחבב, and כ from מכפר.

phrases.english: it endears, it atones.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another explanation of a word, following the earlier ones about אלמנה and מטר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word מזבח hints at four things: מזיח, מזין, מחבב, מכפר.

steps.title: Aren't removing and atoning the same thing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי אלעזר lists both מכפר and מזיח if they seem to mean the same thing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Atoning is the same as removing!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אלעזר's list. Removing sin and atoning for sin sound like one idea, so why count them as two?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If מזיח means pushing away sins, it is the same as מכפר. The list would then repeat itself, which should not happen.

phrases.english: This is "atones,"
and this is "moves away"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the list from step 30.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's list of four things
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: מזיח and מכפר seem to be the same idea, so the list repeats itself.

steps.title: Removing decrees versus atoning for sins
steps.stepSummary: מזיח means the altar removes harsh decrees, and מכפר means it atones for sins.
steps.simpleTranslation: It removes decrees, and it atones for sins.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two words mean different things: one is about decrees, the other is about sins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מזיח is about cancelling bad decrees that were set against people. מכפר is about wiping away the sins themselves. So the list has four different items after all.

keyTerms.meaning: Harsh decrees, punishments that were decided

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר: the מזבח removes harsh decrees, feeds the world, makes Israel beloved, and atones for sins.

phrases.english: It moves away decrees,
and it atones for sins.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 31.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The two words are shown to mean different things
steps.terutzHavaAmina: מזיח and מכפר both mean removing sin.
steps.terutzMaskana: מזיח removes decrees, and מכפר atones for sins.

steps.title: Five effects of dates
steps.stepSummary: רב חנא בגדתאה lists what dates do for the body.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנא בגדתאה said: dates warm the body, fill a person up, loosen the bowels and give strength, but they do not pamper.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another saying of רב חנא בגדתאה, this time about dates.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This continues the pattern of step 28, where רב חנא בגדתאה listed the benefits of rain. Here he lists four good effects of dates and adds one thing they do not do: they do not pamper.

phrases.english: And Rav Chana of Baghdad said:
Dates warm and satisfy,
loosen the bowels, strengthen,
but do not pamper.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new saying by the same speaker as step 28, now about dates.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dates warm, satisfy, loosen the bowels and strengthen, but do not pamper.

steps.title: Someone who ate dates should not rule
steps.stepSummary: רב says that a person who ate dates should not issue a halachic ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: someone who ate dates should not give halachic rulings.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives a rule: after eating dates, a person should not issue a halachic decision.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב treats dates as something that can affect the mind. That makes a person who just ate them unfit to rule for the moment. This sets up the contradiction in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: He should not issue a halachic ruling

phrases.english: Rav said:
One who ate dates should not issue rulings.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: אָכַל תְּמָרִים אַל יוֹרֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of dates with a practical halachic rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who ate dates should not issue halachic rulings.

steps.title: A ברייתא praises dates
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא describes dates as very good, especially at noon, which seems to contradict רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged him: dates are good in the morning and evening and bad in the afternoon. At noon nothing compares to them, and they remove three things: bad thoughts, stomach illness and hemorrhoids.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב with a ברייתא that speaks very highly of dates.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says dates even remove a troubling thought, so they seem to help the mind. If dates are that good, why should eating them stop someone from ruling?

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection (from a ברייתא)

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
Dates in the morning and evening are good;
in the afternoon, they are bad.
At noon, there is nothing like them,
and they remove three things:
a bad thought, stomach illness, and hemorrhoids!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's rule from step 34.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's rule that one who ate dates should not rule
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא presents dates as very good, even clearing the mind of bad thoughts, so they should not disqualify a person from ruling.

steps.title: Healthy but briefly confusing, like wine
steps.stepSummary: Dates really are good, but right after eating them they cloud the mind for a short time, just like wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did we say they are not excellent? They are excellent, but for the moment they confuse the mind. It is like wine, as the master said: one who drinks a רביעית of wine should not give halachic rulings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that both sources are true: dates are healthy, but they briefly affect the mind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב never said dates are bad. His point is only about the short time right after eating, when the mind is unsettled. Wine is similar: it can be good, yet after a רביעית one should not rule.

keyTerms.meaning: They are excellent, of high quality
A quarter-לוג, a set liquid measure

phrases.english: Did we say that they are not excellent?
They certainly are excellent,
but for the moment they confuse the mind.
It is just like wine.
As the master said:
One who drinks a רביעית of wine should not issue rulings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 35.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Both sources are true: long-term benefit versus short-term effect on the mind
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since רב disqualifies a person who ate dates from ruling, we thought he held that dates are bad.
steps.terutzMaskana: Dates are healthy, but right after eating they briefly unsettle the mind, like wine.

steps.title: Before bread or after bread
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: dates eaten before bread are harmful, and dates eaten after bread are good, as אביי's mother taught.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you can say there is no contradiction: one source is about eating dates before bread, the other about eating them after bread. As אביי said, my mother told me: dates before bread are like an axe to a palm tree; after bread they are like a bolt to a door.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another way to resolve the contradiction: it depends on when the dates are eaten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's warning is about dates eaten before a meal, on an empty stomach, when they cause harm. The ברייתא's praise is about dates eaten after bread. אביי's mother compares dates before bread to an axe that cuts and dates after bread to a bolt that holds a door firm.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you prefer, say (introduces another answer)

phrases.english: And if you prefer, say: it is not difficult.
This one is before bread;
phrases.notes: This is רב's warning not to rule after eating dates.

phrases.english: that one is after bread.
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא that praises dates.

phrases.english: As אביי said: My mother told me:
Dates before bread
are like an axe to a palm tree.
After bread,
they are like a bolt to a door.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the challenge of step 35, offered instead of step 36.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The two sources speak about different cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources seemed to describe the same act of eating dates.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב means dates eaten before bread, which are harmful; the ברייתא means dates eaten after bread, which are good.
steps.whatToRemember: Two answers reconcile רב with the ברייתא: dates are healthy but briefly cloud the mind, like wine; or dates before bread harm and dates after bread help.

steps.title: Word breakdowns for door, ladder and bed
steps.stepSummary: Because the word דשא came up, the גמרא explains דשא, דרגא and פוריא as short forms of longer phrases, then introduces a new statement by רב נחמן בר יצחק.
steps.simpleTranslation: About דשא, רבא said: it stands for 'the way through there.' About דרגא, רבא said: 'the way to the roof.' About פוריא, רב פפא said: it is where people are fruitful and multiply. רב נחמן בר יצחק said:
steps.whatsHappening: The word דשא (door) from אביי's mother leads the גמרא into breaking several Aramaic words into the phrases they stand for. The last line introduces a new saying that continues on the next part of the daf.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same style of reading as step 30, where מזבח was read as a short form of four words. Each word is matched to a phrase describing its use: a door is a way through, a ladder is a way to the roof, and a bed is where a couple has children.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new topic about doors or beds. The גמרא is just playing off the word דשא that came up in אביי's mother's saying.

phrases.english: About 'door,' רבא said:
phrases.notes: This picks up the word דשא from אביי's mother's saying in step 37.

phrases.english: It stands for 'the way through there.'

It stands for 'the way to the roof.'
About 'bed,' רב פפא said:
It is where people are fruitful and multiply.
רב נחמן בר יצחק said:
phrases.notes: His statement comes right after this, on the next part of the daf.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Triggered by the word דשא at the end of step 37; uses the same short-form reading style as step 30.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דשא stands for דרך שם, דרגא for דרך גג, and פוריא for פרין ורבין עליה.
